newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Ansett seen back in profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Ansett seen back in profit.

text.p: Ansett Australia executive chairman Ken Cowley said on Sunday he was confident the airline had turned the corner and would be back in profit this year.
"We are trading better," Cowley said in an interview on Channel Nine's Business Sunday programme.
"There's been an enormous amount of work done since the new executive team has been in place and an excellent amount of work in the way we run the company, our cost structure," he said.
"So there are trend lines going in savings, revenues are up... so I think by the end of the first half we would be back in the black," Cowley said.
"...Unless there is something dramatic in front of us in this financial year, we are very determined and dedicated to making a profit this year, modest as it may be," he said.
Cowley said Ansett was still seeking approval for daily flights to Japan and Hong Kong.
The airline, which currently has five flights a week to Hong Kong and Japan (Kansai), also flies to Seoul, Taipei, Kuala Lumpur, Jakarta and Bali.
He said the airline also continued to focus on cutting costs to improve profitability.
Cowley is also chairman of News Corp Ltd subsidiary News Ltd which owns 50 percent of Ansett. The other half is owned by Air New Zealand Ltd.

Ansett, which has recently begun to fly international as well as domestic routes, posted an operating loss before tax of A$18.6 million for the year to June 30 compared with a profit of A$98.5 million in 1994/95.
Revenue for the latest year totalled A$3.30 billion, up from A$3.13 billion a year earlier.
The airline carried 12.16 million passengers in the latest financial year compared with 11.83 million a year earlier.
Ansett earlier this year signed up Cathay Pacific managing director Rod Eddington to take over as executive chairman, replacing Cowley who will remain a director.
Eddington takes up his post in January.
